persona.name: Laura Bennett
persona.usage_pattern: Uses ChatGPT to summarize customer interviews, discovery notes, and client documents.

creation_inputs.notes: This sample demonstrates that Rubricks can start from expert answers and does not require polished reference documents or real examples at setup.

rubrick_entries.title: Claims must be evidence-backed
rubrick_entries.guidance: Any important customer claim, pain point, or product recommendation should be supported by a quote, transcript detail, source evidence, or clearly marked as inference.

rubrick_entries.title: Do not overstate demand
rubrick_entries.guidance: Do not convert one customer's interest into broad demand or roadmap priority unless supported by multiple examples or prior research.

rubrick_entries.title: Preserve objections and hesitation
rubrick_entries.guidance: Customer hesitation, concerns, constraints, and objections should be included and not softened into generic positivity.

rubrick_entries.title: Separate facts, interpretation, and recommendation
rubrick_entries.guidance: The summary should distinguish between what the customer said, what the reviewer inferred, and what the product team may do next.

rubrick_entries.title: Next steps must be actionable
rubrick_entries.guidance: Next steps should be specific, proportional to the evidence, and oriented around validation when confidence is limited.

rubrick_entries.title: Include uncertainty where evidence is limited
rubrick_entries.guidance: If conclusions are based on a single interview or incomplete evidence, the summary should include a confidence level or limitation.

review_items.title: Executive Summary
review_items.suggested_edit: Replace broad demand language with a narrower statement: the customer expressed interest in alerts but raised concerns about data freshness and alert fatigue. Add confidence: Medium, based on one interview.

review_items.title: Customer Pain Points
review_items.suggested_edit: Add the customer's concern that alerts will be ignored if they are not based on current data, and include the need for configurable thresholds.

review_items.title: Product Opportunity
review_items.suggested_edit: State that Smart Inventory Alerts are a promising area for further validation, not a confirmed roadmap priority.

review_items.title: Recommended Next Steps
review_items.suggested_edit: Recommend testing alert explanations with 3–5 similar users before committing to Q3 roadmap scope. Avoid recommending automated reorder suggestions until trust and approval requirements are validated.

starter_cases.title: AI summary overstates customer demand
starter_cases.example_summary: The customer is highly interested and ready to move forward next quarter, with strong demand across teams.
starter_cases.ai_draft_review: Claims must be evidence-backed; demand is overstated.

starter_cases.title: Summary misses customer objection
starter_cases.example_summary: The client responded positively to the proposal and is open to the recommended rollout plan.
starter_cases.ai_draft_review: Preserve hesitation and constraints; key objection is missing.

starter_cases.title: Recommendation lacks next-step owner
starter_cases.example_summary: The best next step is to follow up and move the opportunity ahead after internal review.
starter_cases.ai_draft_review: Actionability gap; next-step owner is unclear.

enriched_outputs.overall_recommendation: Revise before sharing with client team

suggested_work_items.title: Validate alert fatigue concern
suggested_work_items.description: Ask 3–5 similar customers what makes alerts trustworthy versus noisy.

suggested_work_items.title: Prototype alert explanation logic
suggested_work_items.description: Test whether showing current stock, sales velocity, supplier lead time, and promotion context improves trust.
